note: Filled in from docs/accessibility-assessment.md after each round of testing.

done.result: axe-core 4.11 ran on every page, at phone and desktop widths, in light and dark schemes, and with each calculator showing a result and an error. It found no violations. Where it could not judge the contrast of some text, a script measured each case, and none was below the required ratio.
done.environment: Chrome 154 on macOS (Apple silicon), driven by script.

done.result: At 320 CSS pixels wide, no page scrolls sideways. Wide tables and charts scroll inside their own area.
done.environment: Chrome 154 on macOS (Apple silicon), driven by script.

done.result: With the spacing of WCAG 1.4.12 applied, no text was cut off on any page.
done.environment: Chrome 154 on macOS (Apple silicon), driven by script.

done.result: No control is smaller than 24 by 24 CSS pixels, apart from links inside a sentence, which the guidelines exempt, and four standalone links about 21 pixels tall, which pass by the spacing exception of the guideline. Some controls are between 24 and 43 pixels high, below our own aim of 44.
done.environment: Chrome 154 on macOS (Apple silicon), driven by script.

done.result: A script pressed Tab through every page. Every control was reached, in reading order, with an outline style set when focused, and none was covered by other content. A person has not looked at the outline on every control.
done.environment: Chrome 154 on macOS (Apple silicon), driven by script.

done.result: No page skips a heading level.
done.environment: Chrome 154 on macOS (Apple silicon), driven by script.

done.result: Every explanation can be read. With JavaScript off, each calculator shows a notice instead of its form, and none of the sentences that tell a reader what to enter or copy. The triple lock calculator, the rule comparison and the history explorer also show a default result; the budget explorer's notice points to its example budgets, set out in full on its page. Each calculator was also loaded with its own script blocked, when the notice adds that the script did not run and how to report it, and with its script held back, when neither the form nor the notice shows until it runs.
done.environment: Chrome 155 on macOS (Apple silicon), driven by script.

not_done.reason: VoiceOver is the screen reader built into Apple devices. Not yet tested by a person. This needs someone to listen to each page and each calculator.
NVDA is a free screen reader for Windows. Not yet tested. No Windows computer was available.
The keyboard check was made by a script. A person has not yet worked through each calculator with a keyboard alone.

not_done.check: Zoom to 200% and 400% in a browser
not_done.reason: Reflow was measured at the equivalent width by script. A person has not yet zoomed each page in a browser.
Tested at phone width on a computer only, not on a phone.
All checks so far used Chrome.

not_done.check: Use by disabled and older readers
not_done.reason: We have held no usability sessions.
No one has carried one out.

not_done.check: The "Out of date" note in the calculators
not_done.reason: Added on 5 October 2026. When a figure is half typed, the last result stays with this note. It was looked at in screenshots. The automated rules did not scan that state, and nobody has heard it with a screen reader.

not_done.check: Changes to a form when a choice is made
not_done.reason: Some choices change other fields at once: the household, the budget period, the scenario, the number of years, the first year and the pension series. A person has not yet judged whether each change is clear.
